Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: full-bleed conceptual worldbuilding illustration for an illustrated atlas, 1536x1024 landscape.
Primary request: a single polished three-panel narrative image showing the SAME recognizable reusable steel structural bay through THREE SUCCESSIVE LIVES IN TIME: inhabited garden pavilion; careful disassembly and inspection; a new public music room assembled from those same members. Three equally wide vertical panels edge to edge with thin cream gutters, no textual labels and no arrows. Each panel is an architectural scene, not a stockpile. The recurring identity must be instantly visible in all three panels.

Recurring component: one modest four-meter-wide rectangular steel portal with two pale grey square-section uprights and a single pale grey horizontal beam, joined with distinctive indigo blue bolted endplates. A small indigo blue triangular gusset plate with ONE large circular opening sits just below its upper-left corner. Repeat the same proportions, blue joints, circular opening and subtle worn patch in all three panels. Keep its finite size and quantity stable.

Left panel: eye-level view into a modest public garden pavilion beneath this unmistakable portal. Its removable timber roof slats shade a table and a few people sharing tea, vines and mature greenery around the pavilion, warm living materials, pale exposed steel, a recognizable blue circular-opened plate near the left beam-column connection. Light, flourishing, loved, inhabited. No huge building dominating the composition.

Center panel: same bay during a later reuse operation in a clearly closed small work zone. Roof slats have been removed and are stacked neatly. One blue-ended horizontal member is held level by two visible lifting slings suspended from a compact hoist; the two matching uprights rest in cradles nearby. A compact robotic manipulator handles a connector beside the bay, outside any public route. A technician in appropriate workwear checks the retrieved pieces at a staging bench; a small shallow tray contains a few discarded old black seals and worn fasteners separately from the large intact reusable steel members. Keep the distinctive indigo triangular plate with round opening physically attached to the same end of the main member, visible to the reader. Warm daylight, orderly reuse, people and robots perform complementary roles in this proposed world.

Right panel: later, the same indigo-jointed steel portal, same proportions and round-opening gusset, now supports the entrance and front edge of a small public room for live music and embodied expression. The interior arrangement, removable wall panels and fabric acoustic curtain differ from the original open pavilion, while every key steel member remains recognizable. A seated cellist, a standing percussionist, and a few neighbors enjoying the intimate performance. The same finite frame has become a different useful place. The lively interior contrasts with the first garden use.

Style: high-quality architectural narrative concept painting with realistic human scale, convincing steel connections and tactile detail, gentle filmic sunlight; the warm natural greens, pale exposed structural steel, timber and cream tones of an advanced garden district. This is a proposed conceptual sequence, not an engineering drawing.
Constraints: no captions, numbers, letters, logos, watermark, floating UI, arrows or abstract recycling symbols. Do not show three copies in a single simultaneous place; use explicit separate panels and changing surroundings to make successive time readable. Avoid impossible lifting, severed beams, melting or magical mass growth. People have natural faces and hands.

Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: embodied worldbuilding concept image for an illustrated atlas, 1536x1024 landscape.
Primary request: one intimate yet spatially clear scene of neighbors revising a building proposal to preserve a mature community garden. Make collective judgment visible through hands changing a PHYSICAL ARCHITECTURAL MODEL. Their machines can build quickly; their attention decides what should remain. This is a hopeful, concrete moment of world authorship and care, not a protest or staged corporate presentation.

Viewpoint: eye level beside a large waist-height timber model table on the garden's broad pale stone terrace, close enough to see careful hands moving a single reusable miniature structural bay. About six diverse neighbors, younger adult, elder, and a quiet seated listener, thoughtfully absorbed without performative smiles or identical poses. The elder points to the real mature tree beyond the table, another participant listens, and the closest hand slowly places a blue-jointed miniature steel bay into a new set-back position. A wheelchair user comfortably reaches the model from its open edge. Show the model and faces prominently in the foreground.

Model geometry: a detailed physical scale model of this exact mature garden occupies most of the tabletop. A large miniature spreading tree stands in the center of a green garden island. Its protected root zone is a clean circular pale brown translucent ground disc integrated into the model. Existing low garden terraces and paths remain. To one side, a proposed pale steel and timber public room is made of removable rectangular frame modules, with small indigo joint plates. Clearly leave generous open space around the tree and root disc. Two frame modules are lifted out and placed in an orderly tray at the edge; the active hand is setting a remaining bay farther from the root disc. A faint simple outlined footprint on the tabletop shows where the too-large initial proposal would have encroached. No written plans or charts. The physical change must be legible: less building footprint beside the tree, an inhabited garden retained.

Real environment: the full-size version of the same old spreading tree and its garden are immediately behind the table. Dense shade, thick trunk, comfortable bench, rill or low water edge, people sitting quietly under the canopy. In the middle distance a modest demarcated construction site with a compact idle robotic manipulator and neatly racked reusable pale steel members waits beyond the garden, separated from its roots and paths. Two- or three-level lightweight pale steel and timber architecture with lush planted terraces surrounds the scene, coherent with an advanced garden district. The robot is subordinate in the composition, parked calmly: no destruction, extraction, or dystopia.

Lighting and materials: warm dappled midmorning, tactile wood, weathered stone, soft muted greens, cream exposed steel, a few indigo connector details. Cinematic architectural narrative painting with realistic people, plausible hands and model scale, fine readable detail in the model, contemplative warmth. The emotional focus is listening, revising, preserving continuity while retaining the ability to build.
Constraints: no legible or fake text, words, arrows, numbers, logos, banners, protest imagery, holographic interfaces or watermarks. No powerful central leader telling everyone what to do. No felled trees or active machine near roots. Depict a proposed worldbuilding episode, not documentary evidence or an engineering-validated arrangement.
